definitions.gloss: that's right; yes, that's so (Kansai dialect)
definitions.explanation: Kansai (especially Osaka/Kyoto) dialect equivalent of standard そうだ. Used to confirm, agree, or affirm a statement. Also used as an exclamation of sudden recollection ('Oh right!', 'That's it!').

examples.japanese: A:「{昨日|きのう}{大阪|おおさか}に{行|い}ったの?」B:「そうや、{久|ひさ}しぶりに{行|い}ってん。」
examples.english: A: 'Did you go to Osaka yesterday?' B: 'Yeah, I went for the first time in a while.'

examples.japanese: そうや!{鍵|かぎ}、{車|くるま}の{中|なか}に{忘|わす}れてきた。
examples.english: Oh right! I left my keys in the car.

examples.japanese: 「そうやそうや、それが{一番|いちばん}{大事|だいじ}なことやんか。」
examples.english: 'Yes, yes, that's the most important thing, isn't it.'

notes:
Kansai dialect form of そうだ, used primarily in the Osaka/Kyoto/Kobe area. Very common in casual conversation and frequently heard in Kansai-dialect comedy and drama.

COMMON VARIANTS:
- そうやな: right, isn't it (= そうだね)
- そうやんか: that's the way it is, you know
- そうやで: yeah, that's right (emphatic)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- そうだ (standard): that's right — the standard Japanese equivalent
- そうやね: similar, adds seeking-agreement nuance (→ see separate entry)
